pageCache.text:
Reading
England
59Secondary Students
“Reading campus is an excellent place to work, largely due to the supportive community, eager students, excellent facilities, and collaborative team.”
Just minutes from Reading’s bustling heart and its central railway hub, OneSchool Global’s Reading campus serves our dynamic community of 93 students and 20 dedicated educators. The campus’ interior unfolds across multiple levels, featuring light-filled classrooms, collaborative zones, and state-of-the-art learning spaces.
The campus has a rich history, and originally located on the ‘Stoke Poges and Wexham Elementary Schools’ built in 1875. A huge renovation project sympathetically restored the original Grade II listed building to a state-of-the-art learning centre. In late 2019, the school moved to a new location, bringing primary and secondary campuses together.
OneSchool Global Reading Campus fosters a nurturing and dynamic environment, where students’ strong enthusiasm for learning contributes to a vibrant and engaging culture. Our teachers foster students to become leaders of their own learning – self-disciplined, ready to explore and open-minded.

From classroom to career: how OneSchool Global prepared Laura for the real world
Australia
Graduates
SHARE
When Laura Clark reflects on her time at OneSchool Global (OSG), she doesn’t remember formulas or history essays as much as she remembers the skills that have stayed with her throughout her career: discipline, time management, organisation and self-motivation. Today, those same skills help her balance business ownership, family life and leading day-to-day operations at Zed Gifting, a corporate gifting company she now owns.
Laura attended OSG’s former Warrnambool campus before becoming one of the first students at the Mount Gambier campus, which later went on to merge with our Hamilton campus in 2020. Attending a smaller campus gave Laura the opportunity to further develop her skills in being a self-starter and an independent learner. Most of her senior classes were with teachers beyond her home campus, and her success relied on staying organised, managing her own schedule and taking ownership of her learning.
“It wasn’t just sitting there,” Laura recalls. “If I wanted to do well, I had to do the work.”
That self-directed approach became one of the greatest advantages she carried into the workforce.
Building a career through experience
After graduating from OneSchool Global, Laura went on to complete a Diploma in Accounting. From there, she joined a small business where she quickly gained hands-on experience across almost every area of the organisation – from dispatch and customer service to administration and operations. When the business was later acquired, Laura progressed into the role of National Customer Service Manager, a position she thoroughly enjoyed. Along the way, she also developed experience in marketing and sales, building a broad skillset that continues to benefit her today.
Today, Laura brings all of those experiences together as the owner of Zed Gifting, a business specialising in thoughtful corporate gifting experiences that help organisations strengthen relationships with employees and clients. Rather than simply selling gift hampers, Laura works closely with businesses to understand their brand, goals and recipients before designing meaningful gifting experiences that leave a lasting impression. Her role spans customer service, supplier management, logistics, administration and operations, with no two days looking the same.
“I love sitting down with clients, understanding what they’re trying to achieve and then bringing all the pieces together,” Laura says.
“From sourcing products to coordinating suppliers and making sure everything arrives at the right place at the right time, it’s incredibly rewarding seeing it all come together.”
Skills that last beyond the classroom
Looking back, Laura believes the biggest lessons she gained from OSG weren’t found in a textbook.
“School’s not just about maths and English,” she says. “The things that stay with you are the discipline, the time management, the planning and learning to show up and do the work. Those are the skills that stay with you for life.”
She credits OSG’s learning environment with helping her become comfortable managing competing priorities, staying accountable and working independently – qualities that have proven invaluable throughout her career and now as a business owner balancing work and family life.
Advice for today’s students
Laura encourages current OSG students to recognise that every assignment and deadline is helping build habits that will extend far beyond school.
“You might not remember the exact equations you learnt,” she says, “but you’ll remember the discipline you built by showing up, managing your time and doing the work. Those life lessons will stand you in good stead forever.”
For Laura, success hasn’t come from following a single career path. Instead, it’s been about embracing opportunities, continuing to learn and applying the life-ready skills she developed during her time at OSG – skills that have helped her build a rewarding career and confidently navigate the many challenges and opportunities that life has presented along the way.

OSG Ashbrook welcomes new Campus Principal
Our People
Ashbrook
SHARE
Ashbrook is the newest OSG campus in the UK. Located in Coventry, Warwickshire, Ashbrook opened its doors to nearly 200 students in January 2026.
We are now delighted to welcome Mr. Paul Kilbride as Ashbrook’s new campus Principal.
Having started his career as a history teacher, Mr. Kilbride has spent the past 12 years as a head teacher at Old Swinford Hospital School, most recently leading the school’s transition to a co-educational school.
The transition saw the school grow from just under 600 students to over 1,000 students.
As he takes up his new role with OSG, Mr. Kilbride will also mark his 30th year in education.
Mr. Kilbride commented, “I’m very excited about joining OSG. The young people I’ve met here are very impressive, and I’m looking forward to getting to know each student and watching them flourish.
Fundamentally, education is about encouraging students to be the best versions of themselves.”
Mr. Giles Bennett, OneSchool Global Regional Director of Education, commented, ” Mr Kilbride brings a wealth of experience and expertise, built through a distinguished career leading schools with passion, energy and purpose. He has already made a highly positive impression on our school community, quickly building strong relationships with students, staff and families. We are excited about the future under his leadership and look forward to him taking up the role fully in September.”
Mr. Kilbride began his new position on 3 September 2026 as the new school term began.
About OneSchool Global OneSchool Global is an independent school network that has more than 8,000 primary and secondary students and 2,000 staff across the globe, in regions including United Kingdom, North America, Europe, Australia, Argentina, New Zealand and the Caribbean. Our students come from the Plymouth Brethren Christian Church community; however, OneSchool Global is not a religious school and only teaches religion as required in the curriculum.

OneSchool Global’s first Primary LEGO® Lab
Students
Teaching and Learning
SHARE
This year, Primary students across OneSchool Global opened their LEGO® Education SPIKE™ Prime kits, rolled up their sleeves, and discovered just how much they could create when curiosity led the way.
A first for OSG, LEGO® Lab was a hands-on program that ran over several weeks between March and May 2026, giving Primary students a playful, practical route into creativity, problem-solving, coding and teamwork. Working through a sequence of SPIKE™ Prime and Scratch-based activities, students built their confidence, strengthening their Primary Learning to Learn (L2L) skills.
So, what exactly is a SPIKE™ Prime kit? It’s a LEGO® Education set that brings building to life. Students combine familiar LEGO® Technic pieces with motors, sensors and a small programmable hub – the “brain” of each model – then using simple drag-and-drop coding, make their creations move, respond and solve problems. In other words, the models the children built didn’t just sit on the desk; they could be programmed to do a real job!
The program culminated in a ‘final design challenge’, where teams had to solve a real-world problem using their kits. It wasn’t always smooth – and that was rather the point.
Students had to demonstrate resilience as they edited their code again and again until, at last, their robot executed the correct sequence of activities.
“What I loved most was watching children take charge of their own learning,” said Rachel Beyer, OSG’s Global Director of Teaching and Learning (Primary).
“From planning an idea, testing it, watching it not quite work, and going straight back in to try again – that’s curiosity and resilience in action, and it’s exactly what we hoped LEGO® Lab would spark.”
Each campus chose one winning team, and our Student Leadership Teams filmed every design for regional judging.
Celebrating our regional winners
Congratulations to the teams who took top honours in their region!
“High-quality learning doesn’t always start with content – it starts with a good challenge and the freedom to think. Seeing our youngest students code, collaborate and problem-solve their way through the Final Design Challenge was a real joy. A huge thank you to our Primary teams for making it happen,’ said Rachel.
“Thank you to our teachers, regional teams and support staff for the energy and imagination they poured into bringing LEGO® Lab to life. And to our students, for diving in with such enthusiasm and persistence. Here’s to the next build!”
Watch the highlights from every region in our Primary LEGO® Lab video below.

OneSchool Global’s Learning to Learn Framework wins global award for education design
Teaching and Learning
SHARE
OneSchool Global (OSG) has been celebrated on the international stage, receiving a prestigious Silver A’ Design Award for its innovative Learning to Learn framework.
The A’Design Award and Competition recognises exceptional design excellence in products, projects and services, and OSG has received the Silver Award for its excellence in education design.
OSG is one of the world’s largest global school networks, delivering its student-directed learning model to 8,000 students across more than 120 campuses in 20 countries.
Chris O’Reilly, OneSchool Global Acting Global Head of Education, said the recognition reflects the organisation’s commitment to its founding vision.
“OneSchool Global was founded on a vision of high-quality education that enables students to learn how to learn and achieve the best possible outcomes,” Mr O’Reilly said.
“Our Learning to Learn framework brings that vision to life and was developed to increase student engagement and independence.
“Built around three key components, Assignment, Lesson and Study, the framework is a structured yet flexible model that empowers students to take greater ownership of their learning.”
Dr Selina Samuels, international education expert and the author of the Learning to Learn Framework, said that the framework is applicable to all curricula, built on robust structures and practices, and informed by research and educational strategies that are proven to be successful.
“I think the real innovation of the framework is being able to deliver a consistently high quality of teaching and learning across multiple regions and campuses while also ensuring each student’s learning needs are met, giving all students the opportunity to be active and successful learners,” Dr Samuels said.
The A’ Design Award and Competition is one of the world’s largest international design programs, attracting entries from across multiple disciplines and countries each year.
Submissions are evaluated through a blind peer-review process by an expert jury of academics, design professionals and members of the international press.
The Silver A’ Design Award is presented to a select group of top-performing entries, recognising projects that demonstrate a high level of innovation, functionality and impact within their category.
